title: Annotatio III §.III close: Fathers on earthly and heavenly Eucharist — substance remains; later ‘bread changed like Moses’ staff’ phrases — Crocius; stop before §.IV
pass_a_gloss: Irenaeus says: the Eucharist consists of two things, Earthly and Heavenly, and Epiphanius and Theodoret clearly say that the nature and substance remain, and that nevertheless with the Bread gifts are given to us, namely the Body and blood of Christ. Afterwards new manners of speaking were introduced: that the Bread is changed, just as the Staff of Moses was changed into a Serpent. Crocius, Commentary on the Augsburg Confession, p. 204.
pass_b_english: Irenaeus says the Eucharist consists of two things, earthly and heavenly; Epiphanius and Theodoret clearly say the nature and substance remain, yet with the bread gifts are given — namely Christ’s body and blood.
Later new phrases came in: that the bread is changed, as Moses’ staff was changed into a serpent (Crocius on the Augsburg Confession, p. 204).
source_text: Irenaeus inquit: Eucharistia constat duabus rebus, Terrena & Coelesti, & Epiphanius ac Theodoretus clarè dicunt, quod natura & substantia maneat, & quod tamen cum Pane dona nobis dentur, videlicet Corpus & sanguis Christi. Postea nova locutiones introductae sunt: Panem mutari, sicut Baculus Mosis mutabatur in Serpentem. Crocius Comment. in August. Confess. pag. 204.
